providers.name: Rijksarchief / Archives de l'État
providers.what: The State Archives of Belgium, which hold the parish registers and the civil status registers for the whole country — the thing a Belgian search actually needs, and which this atlas was pointing at Geneanet for. WHAT WAS VERIFIED AND WHAT WAS NOT, on 23 Sep 2026: arch.be itself opens. Its genealogical search has moved to agatha.arch.be, which arch.be links to and which would not answer us at all — it completes a TLS handshake and then closes the connection, to a script and to a browser alike. The old host, search.arch.be, is retired and answers 200 for every path with an end-of-life notice, including the three URLs the State Archives' own «Search engines» page still links to. `account` is the class because consulting the scans requires a free registration; that is documented rather than tested here, and this note is the honest record of which.

providers.name: Archieven.nl
providers.what: One search across more than ninety Dutch archives — 133 million person records, 59,308 inventories, and the finding aids themselves rather than only the indexed names. It is the layer above WieWasWie: WieWasWie tells you a birth was registered, this tells you which shelf the register sits on and what else that archive holds about the family. Free to search; whether the scan behind a hit opens depends on the institution that holds it, and this atlas has not walked all ninety.

providers.name: Archion

providers.name: Internet Archive

providers.name: Archives New Zealand — Collections
providers.what: New Zealand probate, military and immigration records, much of it digitised and free.

providers.name: Archiwum Państwowe w Bydgoszczy
providers.what: The Polish state archive for the Kuyavian-Pomeranian voivodeship, holding the civil registers of the former Prussian registry offices of the region, Szubin among them. IT ANSWERS LETTERS AND WILL SHARE SCANS: three e-mails in September 2026 were each answered within about eight days, in Polish, over the Director's signature with a named case officer. It points first at genealogiawarchiwach.pl for what is already digitised, and then supplied a 103-scan volume that is NOT on that portal, shared from its own OneDrive. TWO HOLDINGS FACTS IT STATED BY LETTER THAT NO ONLINE CATALOGUE SHOWS: the metrical books of the Jewish religious community of Szubin survive ONLY for 1820-1847; and the alphabetical death indexes (skorowidze zgonów) of USC Szubin Miasto survive ONLY for 1874-1878 and 1894-1924, with nothing between. An archivist there will also read a difficult line from a register on request and say plainly where the reading is uncertain.

providers.name: Lietuvos archyvai (Lithuanian State Archives)

providers.name: ARHiNET — Croatian State Archives
providers.what: The Croatian State Archives, and through it the national register of archival fonds — which archive holds which fonds; the paper itself is almost all unphotographed. THE OLD LINK HERE WAS DEAD. This row pointed at arhinet.arhiv.hr, which no longer resolves at all — NXDOMAIN on Google's and Cloudflare's resolvers both, not a timeout or a redirect, so every Croatian researcher who clicked ARHiNET on this map got nothing. The successor is HAIS at hais.arhiv.hr, which resolves to 161.53.80.20 and did not answer this project's requests at all; unable to tell a service that is down from one that does not answer us, this points at the archive's own site, which does answer, rather than shipping a second link nobody can open.

providers.name: Arhiv Vojvodine

providers.name: Agenția Națională a Arhivelor (Moldova)
providers.what: Moldova's National Archives Agency. OPENED 2026-09-29: it publishes ONLINE INVENTORIES — its own front page announces inventories for the Soviet period 1917–1940 — and a separate notice about restoring access to its digital collections, so images may exist beyond the finding aids; that part is not confirmed and the access class here describes the inventories, which are. providers.name: Catholic Metropolitan Cemeteries Trust — Brisbane (cemsearch)
providers.what: The burial register search for the Roman Catholic cemeteries of the Archdiocese of Brisbane, Nudgee among them — NINE cemeteries. Returns register number, cemetery, name, birth, death, interment date and PLOT NUMBER. It is NOT in the Brisbane City Council grave search, because these are not council cemeteries: a family buried here is invisible to the council portal and to the aggregators that copy it. Queried by POST to `query.php?type=Deceased` with `CemeteryCode=%` and `SectionCode=%` — passing «All» returns nothing. Used from the Falco family archive, where it produced five burials that corrected two death dates carried from a family tree.
providers.triageNote: Added from the Falco family archive, which has used it repeatedly. Access class still needs a person: it answers without a login, but nobody has surveyed what an ordinary visitor is charged for a full register entry, so it stays unsurveyed. No Wikidata id established for the operating trust and none was guessed.

providers.name: Bristol Archives
providers.what: The city record office for Bristol: Church of England parish registers for the Bristol parishes, plus the city's own papers. The registers themselves are NOT online here — they are filmed on Ancestry, behind a subscription. What this office does do is read an entry for you: a seven-part enquiry about one 1828 marriage register entry was answered in nine days, in full, FREE, by staff who had viewed the record. Their quoted research service is £13 for up to half an hour and was not charged. The reply also corrected a surname spelling that two index sites had both transcribed the same way, and volunteered a later record that had not been asked about. Worth writing to.
providers.triageNote: Added from the D'Arcy archive after a free lookup answered in nine days. access=onsite: the paper is in the building and the films are on a commercial site.

providers.name: Bundesarchiv
providers.what: The German Federal Archives. Civil and military administration of the Prussian provinces, the wartime records, and the card indexes of the expelled — much of it for ground that is no longer German.

providers.name: CEMLA — Centro de Estudios Migratorios Latinoamericanos
providers.what: Buenos Aires port arrival books, 1882–1960, indexed by passenger name. Worked by the Blažević archive across four spellings of the same surname — which is how it has to be worked, because the clerk wrote what he heard. Not yet surveyed. NO SEAT RECORDED, DELIBERATELY. This is the one row the source-layer audit's `at` finding genuinely applies to — every other row it named is a COUNTRYWIDE kind, which sourcesNear() exempts from distance sorting, so a missing seat costs them nothing. CEMLA is filed as an index and is sorted by distance, and it does sink. Its Wikidata item (Q140429797) states a country, a founding year and a website and NO coordinates, so there is nothing to write: the institute is in Buenos Aires by its own description, which is prose and not a claim, and a coordinate inferred from prose is the guess this project refuses.
providers.triageNote: Added from the family research archives, which record work actually done here. Access class still needs a person.

providers.name: Državni arhiv u Zadru
providers.what: The Zadar State Archive, which holds the Venetian and Austrian registers of Dalmatia — including parishes whose books never went to Split. Its own analytical inventory (HR-DAZD-378, ~2,400 civil-registry books) states the collection's scope explicitly: coastal Dalmatia from Rab in the north to Hvar and Vis in the south. Confirmed by walking the inventory's full parish list: it holds NOTHING for the inland Lika-Senj cluster (Sveti Rok, Lovinac, Gračac, Ričice, Donji Lapac, Gospić) — those parishes are out of scope for this archive, not merely unindexed. The site itself blocks automated/headless browsing (403) but loads normally in an ordinary browser. Its analytical inventory HR-DAZD-378 (Burić and Modrinić, 2014) is now held in data/dazd-378-registers.json: 178 parishes and 1,840 register books with the archive's own signatures, which is what a letter here has to quote.

BT 27 IS NOT ONE FORM AND ITS COLUMNS ARE NOT A CONSTANT. The outward passenger lists were re-drawn across the series, so a field present in one piece proves nothing about another and the era has to be checked before a row is planned around it. Sampled by the Luwinski archive: the 1907 form has NO «last address in the United Kingdom» column at all and buckets ages by nationality instead; the 1937 and 1939 form — printed «P.M. 21», columns (1)–(9) — carries last UK address at (6), country of last permanent residence at (8) and country of intended future permanent residence at (9); a 1951 piece is a typed US military transport manifest filed inside BT 27 with none of the Board of Trade form left. ACROSS EVERY REVISION SEEN, none gives an address in the DESTINATION country — the finest is a country and nothing below it, so «where in Australia did they settle» is not a question this series answers.

providers.name: Genealogia w Archiwach
providers.what: A Polish state-archives portal of scanned metrical books — civil registration from the Prussian partition (1874 on), duplicates of Roman Catholic parish registers from before that, and population and registration books from 1837. Separate from Szukaj w Archiwach and run by its own archives. Secondary sources say the scans are free and need no account; NOBODY HERE HAS CONFIRMED THAT, because the site is a Vaadin application that renders nothing without JavaScript, so it is marked unsurveyed rather than taking a blog's word for what it costs. SCANS ARE SERVED BY A LORIS IIIF IMAGE SERVER and can be read in place without downloading: /loris/<id>/<x,y,w,h>/<width>,/0/default.jpg returns an arbitrary region at up to TWICE native resolution, which is enough to settle a difficult hand. info.json returns 403 while image requests succeed, and anything above 2x returns a bare 404. The viewer's own canvas is tainted, so the tile server is the route and screenshots are not. THE PORTAL WILL NOT OPEN A UNIT BY ITS SIGNATURE: a scan's modal id resolves only inside the current search result set, so a neighbouring scan cannot be reached by guessing an id. The route that works is to open any scan's modal, click 'View the document' to expose the unit's own scan list, click Show on the scan wanted, and take the new Loris id from the network log.

providers.name: Žrtve rata 1941–1945 — Muzej žrtava genocida
providers.what: The Museum of Genocide Victims in Belgrade's name-by-name register of people killed in Yugoslavia between 1941 and 1945 — 659,122 records, free and without an account. Searchable by given name, surname, year of birth, the MUNICIPALITY AND PLACE OF RESIDENCE ON 6 APRIL 1941, and by place, year and circumstances of death; each row also carries the parent's name, place of birth and nationality as recorded. That pre-war residence field is what makes it genealogical rather than commemorative: it places a named person in a named village on a fixed date, which is exactly what a register would give you and often the only thing that survives for these years. Counted as an INDEX — it gives structured records, not images of the documents behind them. Scope is the whole of the former Yugoslavia; the countries listed here are the ones seen in the data (Vukovar and Vinkovci, Zavidovići and Lopare, Sremska Mitrovica), so it will also answer for Montenegro and North Macedonia beyond what has been checked here. The interface is Serbian. Read from the site itself on 2026-09-29; access class confirmed by use, not assumed. HOW TO SEARCH IT WITHOUT READING A FAMILY AS ABSENT. The surname field matches EXACTLY, not as a substring: «Franceschi» returns 0 while «Defranceschi» returns 2, so a stem finds nothing and every prefixed form has to be sent as its own query. And the spellings are not interchangeable — they hold DIFFERENT PEOPLE. «Defranceschi» gives two men at Pula and Vodnjan; «Defrančeški» gives a third at Pazin and Gologorica, and neither query returns the other's records. Query the Italian, the Croatian and the diacritic-stripped forms separately and treat the results as additive. Verified by search on 2026-09-29. One more thing worth knowing: the front end races when queries are run back to back, and can paint one query's rows under another's count, so a count is only trustworthy taken one query per page load.

providers.name: NAAIRS — National Archives of South Africa
providers.what: The South African archives index — estate files above all, which are the backbone of South African genealogy. An index; the file is ordered from the depot. TWO DATABASES SINCE THE 2026 MIGRATION AND ONLY ONE IS COMPLETE: NARSSA's own 'Using the Search Function' page states it is migrating more than 8.3 million entries from the old NAAIRS database to the new one, that the new 'fulltext search' WILL NOT DISPLAY ALL THE RECORDS IN THE SYSTEM, and that 'Search Old NAAIRS database' will provide a more complete search. providers.name: Mi Registro Civil
providers.what: Mexico's Plataforma Nacional del Registro Civil. OPENED 2026-09-29, AND IT IS NOT A GENEALOGICAL SOURCE — worth saying plainly, because its name promises one. It is a SERVICES portal: you pick one of the 32 entidades from a dropdown (Aguascalientes through Zacatecas, plus EXTRANJERO) and it shows the trámites that state offers — ordering a certified copy of a civil record, and checking the status of a request you already made. There is no historical search, no index to browse and no images. Mexican civil registration is administered per state, and this is the front door to thirty-two separate state offices rather than a national record set. Filed as `catalogue` because that is the nearest true class — the paper is not photographed and must be asked for — though even a catalogue is more than it offers.

providers.name: Trove
providers.what: The National Library of Australia's newspaper and gazette archive. Free and full-text. Most titles stop at 1954 for copyright, which is the usual rule of thumb — BUT TWO EXCEPTIONS REACH MUCH LATER AND ARE EASY TO MISS: THE CANBERRA TIMES IS DIGITISED 1926-1995, and the COMMONWEALTH OF AUSTRALIA GAZETTE 1901-1973, whose naturalisation and citizenship lists carry name, street address and date. Those two make Trove usable for post-war arrivals that the 1954 rule would rule out. NOTE THAT THE SEARCH NORMALISES SPELLING — two different spellings of one surname can return an identical result set — SO TROVE CANNOT BE USED AS A SPELLING TEST. The v3 API needs an X-API-KEY header and does not serve article text at ordinary key level; the public article page carries the OCR.

providers.name: Cognomix — Mappe dei cognomi italiani
providers.what:
Cognomix — where an Italian surname is, by region. OPENED 2026-09-29 on /mappe-dei-cognomi-italiani/FORNASAR, which reports «circa 25 famiglie Fornasar in Italia» and breaks it down: Piemonte 11, Friuli V.G. 8, Veneto 4, Liguria 1, Puglia 1, drawn on a Leaflet map of Italy. Free, no account, and the URL takes the surname uppercased, so a page can be linked to directly.
WHAT IT COUNTS IS FAMILIES TODAY, NOT RECORDS. This is the Italian equivalent of the national-register rows this atlas already holds for Croatia, Slovenia and France — «how many people of that name a state counted», the closest thing to «where the name is now» — and the same caveat applies twice over: it says nothing about where a family was in 1780, and a small number tells you as much about the source as about the name. It is an INDEX, not images: there is no register behind it to open.
The page carries heavy third-party advertising, which is worth knowing before sending somebody there but says nothing about the data.
providers.triageNote: Opened on a real surname page (FORNASAR) on 2026-09-29; the distribution and its per-region counts read directly off the page.

providers.name: Državni arhiv u Dubrovniku
providers.what: The state archive of Dubrovnik, in the Sponza palace, holding the records of the Republic of Ragusa, which was its own state until 1808 and kept its own chancery. IMPORTANT, AND THE REASON THIS ROW EXISTS: it NO LONGER HOLDS THE PARISH REGISTERS. A senior archivist there wrote on 28 September 2026 that «Državni arhiv u Dubrovniku predao je sve matične knjige Biskupskom ordinarijatu u Dubrovniku» — all the matične knjige have gone to the Diocesan Ordinariate — and referred the enquiry on. So a register question addressed here is answered with a redirect, and the Republic's own pre-1808 fonds is what this institution is still for.
providers.triageNote: Added from a family archive after a reply from the archive itself. Access class not surveyed. NOTE the atlas's existing asd-ragusa is the Archivio di Stato di RAGUSA IN SICILY, on Antenati — not this. Ragusa is the Italian name of Dubrovnik and the two are a standing trap.

providers.name: Arhiv Dubrovačke biskupije (Biskupski ordinarijat)
providers.what: The diocesan archive of Dubrovnik, and SINCE THE TRANSFER THE HOLDER OF THE CITY'S PARISH REGISTERS: the state archive states it handed over all the matične knjige and gives this as the address for them. Nothing has been asked of it yet, and no statement about what it holds volume by volume, what it charges, or whether it answers by email, is made here — only that it is where the registers went.
